$comment: The mutant ledger for issue #22's realtime layer.
Standing campaign rule, from #21's round-2 gauntlet: a mutation claim ships
with a committed, re-runnable mutant list and its results, or it is not
evidence.
Run it:   node mutants/run.mjs
Gate it:  node mutants/run.mjs --check
Unit only: node mutants/run.mjs --suite unit
Every entry restores a behaviour a later round removed — round 3's, round 2's,
or round 1's where a later round fixed it and this one must not undo it.
`catches` names the tests that must go red and the runner asserts each one did,
so a mutant tripped by something unrelated is recorded as an escape.
`sql` mutants are applied to the live database and undone by re-executing the
statements extracted from the migration each one names — migrations are
journalled, so editing an applied one demonstrates nothing, and a restore that
used a copied string could re-deploy something the repo does not ship. The
migration is named rather than assumed because 0004 and 0005 both define
`atrium_append_core_event`, and restoring from 0004 would silently re-deploy
the eight-argument version this round replaced.
A mutation of a file under `packages/` triggers a workspace rebuild before the
suite and again after the restore: `packages/ingest` and `apps/server` resolve
`@atrium/core` and `@atrium/db` through their built `dist`, so a ledger that
skipped the rebuild would measure the previous artifact (#26 r6).

mutants.why: Round 2's shape: delivery happens only when a notification arrives. The timer that makes the ledger the durable path is gone.
catches: converges with no event bus at all — the reconciler is the durable path

mutants.why: Round 2 had no listener-loss callback. With the timer still running this is a latency regression rather than a correctness one, which is exactly why it needs its own pin: every other reconciliation test stays green.
catches: reconciles on the listener’s resubscribe, not only on the next tick

mutants.why: Removes the unsolicited head frame. `sync` still covers rows this instance never folded; nothing covers a row it folded and broadcast whose frame one socket lost.
catches: tells a subscriber the head even when the event frame itself was lost
converges after an event frame is lost following a fan-out, in a room that goes quiet
repeats the head until the socket acknowledges it, then stops

mutants.why: Round 2's privilege block granted EXECUTE on the append function to PUBLIC, which made the call-stack trigger the guard and the door itself unlocked.
mutants.apply: GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.atrium_append_core_event(uuid, text, event_type, actor_kind, text, jsonb, timestamptz, jsonb, text) TO PUBLIC
catches: is not executable by PUBLIC

mutants.why: Round 2's append function performed no membership authorization at all: any caller that could execute it wrote durable history into any room as any user.
mutants.apply: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.atrium_append_core_event(p_room_id uuid, p_event_id text, p_type event_type, p_actor_kind actor_kind, p_actor_id text, p_payload jsonb, p_occurred_at timestamptz, p_trusted_messages jsonb DEFAULT NULL, p_origin text DEFAULT NULL) RETURNS TABLE ("seq" bigint, "room_seq" bigint) LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $m$ DECLARE v_room_seq bigint; v_seq bigint; v_max_at timestamptz; v_max_id text; BEGIN PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(1096045106::bigint); SELECT e.occurred_at, e.id INTO v_max_at, v_max_id FROM core_events e ORDER BY e.occurred_at DESC, e.id COLLATE "C" DESC LIMIT 1; IF v_max_at IS NOT NULL AND NOT (p_occurred_at > v_max_at OR (p_occurred_at = v_max_at AND (p_event_id COLLATE "C") > (v_max_id COLLATE "C"))) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'out of order' USING ERRCODE = '55000', CONSTRAINT = 'core_events_append_canonical_order'; END IF; SELECT coalesce(max(e.room_seq), 0) + 1 INTO v_room_seq FROM core_events e WHERE e.room_id = p_room_id; INSERT INTO core_events (room_id, room_seq, id, type, actor_kind, actor_id, payload, occurred_at, trusted_messages) VALUES (p_room_id, v_room_seq, p_event_id, p_type, p_actor_kind, p_actor_id, p_payload, p_occurred_at, p_trusted_messages) RETURNING core_events.seq INTO v_seq; PERFORM pg_notify('atrium_ledger', json_build_object('origin', p_origin, 'roomId', p_room_id, 'seq', v_seq, 'roomSeq', v_room_seq)::text); "seq" := v_seq; "room_seq" := v_room_seq; RETURN NEXT; END; $m$
restorePrelude: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.atrium_append_core_event(uuid, text, event_type, actor_kind, text, jsonb, timestamptz, jsonb, text)
catches: refuses a human actor who holds no membership in the room
refuses a human actor id that could not be a member at all

mutants.why: Round 2's append function ran no reducer validation. The reducer refuses an event for exactly two reasons and both are properties of position; without the canonical-order gate a caller can write a row that a replay refuses to fold, and the server then cannot start against its own log.
mutants.apply: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.atrium_append_core_event(p_room_id uuid, p_event_id text, p_type event_type, p_actor_kind actor_kind, p_actor_id text, p_payload jsonb, p_occurred_at timestamptz, p_trusted_messages jsonb DEFAULT NULL, p_origin text DEFAULT NULL) RETURNS TABLE ("seq" bigint, "room_seq" bigint) LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $m$ DECLARE v_room_seq bigint; v_seq bigint; BEGIN PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(1096045106::bigint); IF p_actor_kind = 'human' THEN IF p_actor_id !~ '^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'not a user id' USING ERRCODE = '42501', CONSTRAINT = 'core_events_append_actor_authorized'; END IF; PERFORM 1 FROM memberships m WHERE m.room_id = p_room_id AND m.user_id = p_actor_id::uuid FOR SHARE; IF NOT FOUND THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'no membership' USING ERRCODE = '42501', CONSTRAINT = 'core_events_append_actor_authorized'; END IF; END IF; SELECT coalesce(max(e.room_seq), 0) + 1 INTO v_room_seq FROM core_events e WHERE e.room_id = p_room_id; INSERT INTO core_events (room_id, room_seq, id, type, actor_kind, actor_id, payload, occurred_at, trusted_messages) VALUES (p_room_id, v_room_seq, p_event_id, p_type, p_actor_kind, p_actor_id, p_payload, p_occurred_at, p_trusted_messages) RETURNING core_events.seq INTO v_seq; PERFORM pg_notify('atrium_ledger', json_build_object('origin', p_origin, 'roomId', p_room_id, 'seq', v_seq, 'roomSeq', v_room_seq)::text); "seq" := v_seq; "room_seq" := v_room_seq; RETURN NEXT; END; $m$
restorePrelude: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.atrium_append_core_event(uuid, text, event_type, actor_kind, text, jsonb, timestamptz, jsonb, text)
catches: refuses an event that does not sort strictly after the ledger cursor
breaks an exact timestamp tie on the event id, the way the reducer does

mutants.why: Round 2 emitted pg_notify from the application, so a row written by anything else landed durably and told nobody.
mutants.apply: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.atrium_append_core_event(p_room_id uuid, p_event_id text, p_type event_type, p_actor_kind actor_kind, p_actor_id text, p_payload jsonb, p_occurred_at timestamptz, p_trusted_messages jsonb DEFAULT NULL, p_origin text DEFAULT NULL) RETURNS TABLE ("seq" bigint, "room_seq" bigint) LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $m$ DECLARE v_room_seq bigint; v_seq bigint; v_max_at timestamptz; v_max_id text; BEGIN PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(1096045106::bigint); IF p_actor_kind = 'human' THEN IF p_actor_id !~ '^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'not a user id' USING ERRCODE = '42501', CONSTRAINT = 'core_events_append_actor_authorized'; END IF; PERFORM 1 FROM memberships m WHERE m.room_id = p_room_id AND m.user_id = p_actor_id::uuid FOR SHARE; IF NOT FOUND THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'no membership' USING ERRCODE = '42501', CONSTRAINT = 'core_events_append_actor_authorized'; END IF; END IF; SELECT e.occurred_at, e.id INTO v_max_at, v_max_id FROM core_events e ORDER BY e.occurred_at DESC, e.id COLLATE "C" DESC LIMIT 1; IF v_max_at IS NOT NULL AND NOT (p_occurred_at > v_max_at OR (p_occurred_at = v_max_at AND (p_event_id COLLATE "C") > (v_max_id COLLATE "C"))) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'out of order' USING ERRCODE = '55000', CONSTRAINT = 'core_events_append_canonical_order'; END IF; SELECT coalesce(max(e.room_seq), 0) + 1 INTO v_room_seq FROM core_events e WHERE e.room_id = p_room_id; INSERT INTO core_events (room_id, room_seq, id, type, actor_kind, actor_id, payload, occurred_at, trusted_messages) VALUES (p_room_id, v_room_seq, p_event_id, p_type, p_actor_kind, p_actor_id, p_payload, p_occurred_at, p_trusted_messages) RETURNING core_events.seq INTO v_seq; "seq" := v_seq; "room_seq" := v_room_seq; RETURN NEXT; END; $m$
restorePrelude: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.atrium_append_core_event(uuid, text, event_type, actor_kind, text, jsonb, timestamptz, jsonb, text)
catches: emits the doorbell from inside the function, with the appending origin
rings for everybody when the appender did not name itself

mutants.why: Deletes the inverted r1 major 2. With #21 the payload has no actor, so the old equality became unsatisfiable and the tempting move is to drop it — taking the rule it carried with it.
mutants.apply: ALTER TABLE core_events DROP CONSTRAINT core_events_payload_has_no_actor
catches: refuses an actor inside the payload — there is exactly one, and it is a column

mutants.why: Without it, `{kind:'system', actor_id:'alice'}` is a row that reads as a person having done what the process did.
mutants.apply: ALTER TABLE core_events DROP CONSTRAINT core_events_actor_id_matches_kind
catches: refuses an actor_id that disagrees with its kind

mutants.why: Collapses every catch-up to one page, which is the arrangement under which r2's suite never once ran the catch-up loop against a real database.
catches: drives the production client’s loop to the head across several real pages
says there is more when a page is truncated, and stops when it is not

mutants.why: Round 1's blocking finding, whole: `more` computed from page fullness AND the page and the head read separately. Both halves are needed, and that is the point — with the snapshot read in place an untruncated page always has `to === head`, so r1's arithmetic alone produces the right answer for the wrong reason and escapes. The defect only exists when the two numbers describe two different moments.
catches: never reports a client caught up while the head is ahead of it

mutants.why: Round 2's ordering: mutate the in-memory list, then persist the cursor. A crash in between resumes past an event nothing holds.
catches: resumes at the last entry it durably committed when it dies mid-page
leaves its own cursor where it was when the journal refuses an entry

mutants.why: Round 2's `WatermarkStore` by construction: the cursor is durable and the events are not, so a reload is a room that believes it is up to date and holds nothing.
catches: resumes from a durable journal rather than replaying the room

mutants.why: Leaves a client that lost one event frame with nothing able to tell it, because its cursor and its stale head agree.
catches: asks for the gap when told the room is ahead of its cursor

mutants.why: Without a limit the client takes the server's 1000-entry default, and no fixture in this repo produces a second page.
catches: asks for a bounded page when one is configured

mutants.why: Round 3's inference, from the reconciler's side: a room it just fanned rows out to needs no head frame, 'because its head is announced by construction'. The fan-out is the send that may have been lost, so the room that just received rows is the one most in need of being told where it is.
mutants.replace:
if (head === 0) continue;
      if (folded.some((entry) => entry.roomId === roomId)) continue;
catches: reports the head of a room it just delivered every row of

mutants.why: The timer, the doorbell and a resubscribe can coincide; without coalescing each opens its own pass and they queue on the ledger's in-process mutex for no benefit.
catches: coalesces overlapping passes rather than queueing them

mutants.why: On the timer's un-awaited call an escaping rejection is an unhandled rejection, which `index.ts` answers by exiting the process — so one bad database minute stops the durable path entirely.
catches: survives a failing pass and reconciles again on the next one

mutants.why: The two ledger-only kinds never reach `CoreEvent.parse`, so without this guard they are the one door in the wall — a `message_posted` payload free to carry an actor nothing folds and nothing believes.
catches: refuses an actor inside the payload, for the ledger-only kinds too

mutants.why: #21 made the sentence a render of a structured reason; storing the sentence freezes today's wording into every historical row and makes 'which rule raised this' a substring search over prose.
catches: requires a structured reason on every attention item, not a rendered sentence

mutants.why: r1 major 3, in its live form: a core type the ledger classifies as server-only is never folded and vanishes from every replay while live ingestion still applies it. Pinned by a compile-time parity assert rather than by a test — `packages/db` asserts its enum against @atrium/core's, so the divergence cannot be built, let alone shipped. Declared as `caughtBy: build` because a mutant caught by tsc has not measured any test, and a ledger that let those two look alike would print ticks for rules nothing ran.
A partially written record is the one case where resuming is worse than replaying: the cursor names a position whose event the store does not hold, and the next since asks from past the hole.
mutants.find:
const held = events.at(-1)?.roomSeq ?? 0;
      if (lastSeq !== held) return { events: [], lastSeq: 0 };
catches: reads a torn record as no history at all

mutants.why: Two keys is two writes with no transaction between them — the exact window RoomJournal exists to close, reopened by the one storage API that cannot close it any other way.
mutants.replace:
store.setItem(key(roomId), JSON.stringify({ events: kept, lastSeq }));
          store.setItem(`${key(roomId)}:cursor`, String(lastSeq));
catches: persists the events and the cursor under one key, in one write

mutants.why: Round 3's other half: a per-room latch that suppresses a repeat, so a socket which lost the one frame carrying a head is never told again — the head frame failing in exactly the case it exists for. The latch is hung off the callback rather than declared beside `timer` because a mutant is one substitution; the behaviour is r3's exactly.
catches: reports the head again on a pass where nothing changed

mutants.why: Round 3's blocking defect, whole, expressed in r4's shape: a successful fan-out records an acknowledgement for every subscriber in the room. 'We called broadcast' becomes 'the client has it', and a socket that dropped the frame in a room that then goes quiet is never told again.
catches: converges after an event frame is lost following a fan-out, in a room that goes quiet

mutants.why: The other direction: never record what a client acknowledges, so the head frame is a permanent per-room heartbeat. Correct, and it makes the frame something a client learns to ignore — which is why r3 tried to suppress it in the first place.
catches: repeats the head until the socket acknowledges it, then stops

mutants.why: Two head frames in flight are answered in whatever order the socket delivers them, so a client mid-catch-up answers the first with a cursor it has already passed. Taking the smaller number re-opens frames the client has already answered.
catches: never lets an acknowledgement move backwards

mutants.why: A socket that closes leaves its acknowledgements behind: one entry per connection for the life of the process, with no symptom until the memory is gone.
catches: forgets a socket entirely when it closes

mutants.why: The client half of the acknowledgement. Without it the server never learns what any socket holds and every subscribed room gets a head frame every pass, for ever.
catches: tells the server what it holds every time it is told a head

mutants.why: Acknowledging a page that says `more` claims a position the client has not reached, so the server stops telling a client that is still several pages behind — the premature silence this whole finding is about, arrived at from the client side.
catches: does not acknowledge a catch-up it is still in the middle of

mutants.why: Round 3's blocking 2: the replay reads the receipt window out of `messages` instead of out of the row. `messages.author_id` is ON DELETE SET NULL, so deleting a human author makes an acceptance that folded cleanly replay as a receipt failure — same derivation code, different substrate.
mutants.replace: rows.push({ ...(await trustToRecord(db, entry.event, entry.actor)), event: entry.event });
catches: replays an accepted claim identically after its author is deleted

mutants.why: The other end of the same defect: fold against the window but never write it down. Every fold after the append then has nothing to read, and `null` is the absence #21's reducer refuses — so the row folds one way live and another way for ever after.
catches: replays an accepted claim identically after its author is deleted

mutants.why: Restores r2's has-a-timezone-designator check. Every spelling it admits beyond the canonical one is an instant the SQL gate treats as equal and the reducer treats as a different string, so the two disagree about whether a pair of events is simultaneous.
mutants.apply: ALTER TABLE core_events DROP CONSTRAINT core_events_payload_at_is_canonical_utc; ALTER TABLE core_events ADD CONSTRAINT core_events_payload_at_is_canonical_utc CHECK (core_events.payload->>'at' ~ '(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})$')
restorePrelude: ALTER TABLE core_events DROP CONSTRAINT core_events_payload_at_is_canonical_utc
catches: refuses every spelling of `at` but the canonical one

mutants.why: Without it an astral-plane id reaches the ledger, and the SQL gate's `COLLATE "C"` and the reducer's UTF-16 comparison order it differently — the canonical order stops being one order.
mutants.apply: ALTER TABLE core_events DROP CONSTRAINT core_events_id_is_safe_to_order
catches: refuses an id outside the charset the two orderings agree on
disagrees outside the subset, and the constraints refuse every witness

mutants.why: The snapshot is what a replay folds a receipt against. Without the shape check a writer that is not the server can leave a window a replay cannot read, and the row that folded cleanly live becomes unfoldable.
mutants.apply: ALTER TABLE core_events DROP CONSTRAINT core_events_trusted_messages_shape
catches: refuses a receipt snapshot that is not a list of {id, authorId, body}

mutants.why: r3's journal, unbounded. Not a slow leak: it is a guarantee of reaching the browser's quota on any room that runs long enough, and what happens at that point is the next mutant.
catches: keeps a bounded window rather than growing until the store refuses it

mutants.why: r3's behaviour once the quota is reached: `setItem` throws, `applyEntry` leaves the cursor where it was — correctly, for a transient failure — and a full store is not transient, so the room stops advancing while the socket carries on delivering.
catches: falls back to memory, loudly, when even one entry will not fit
keeps applying events after the journal has degraded

mutants.why: The @atrium/core half of the canonical-ordering subset. Without it the application can mint an id whose UTF-16 order and whose byte order disagree, and only the database CHECK stands between that and a ledger with two orders in it.
catches: refuses an id outside the Basic Multilingual Plane
refuses whitespace, control characters, and an unbounded length
